processes.description: Volume and accounting staff circulate a tentative close schedule for the coming month, then revise and reissue it after discussion with the people involved. During the close, requests go out to clear intercompany items, resolve Sitara volume variances, set up missing deals, report outstanding expenses and confirm last-day files are complete. Treasury-style notices report amounts moved to or released from Schedule C each night, and late differences are investigated before they are written off.
steps: Circulate the tentative close schedule for the coming month.
Revise and reissue the schedule after discussion, including the cut-off after which no changes can be made.
Send lists of deals with volume variances or one-sided entries to schedulers and logistics for correction.
Ask for missing deals to be set up and intercompany balances to be cleared.
Collect outstanding expense items and confirmation that last-day files are complete.
Report nightly amounts moved to or released from Schedule C.
Investigate remaining differences and decide whether to write them off.

stalls.summary: A distributed schedule was unreadable and had to be sent again.
Schedulers were confused about when changes could still be made, so the cut-off had to be restated in a later round.
A request to clear intercompany items went unanswered and needed a follow-up asking whether anyone had looked into it.
Unexplained differences remained open late enough that a write-off was being considered before anyone knew what they related to.

contradictions.summary: An amount announced as taken to Schedule C one night was removed again the next business day, and a different amount was added a month later, so the nightly notices reverse one another.
In the same round, deal setup is assigned to Ami while resolution with Transco is assigned to Charlotte, who is not among the process's participants, leaving the follow-through split.

automation.approach: Publish the close calendar from one shared template with fixed cut-off times, and generate the variance and unmatched-deal list automatically from the deal and volume systems so each scheduler receives only their exceptions. A tracker of open close items (intercompany, expenses, last-day files) would show who has confirmed completion.
automation.rationale: The rounds repeat the same items every month: schedule, cut-off, variances, intercompany, expenses, last-day file. A close checklist with owners and cut-offs addresses the confusion over when changes are allowed and the follow-ups on unanswered items.

work_estimate.rationale: Most rounds involve building or revising a schedule, pulling a list of variance deals or a counterparty breakdown by day, or tracing unexplained differences. Around 45 minutes covers compiling and checking one such list or schedule; the range runs to 120 for rounds that reconcile many deals. Listing variances and building the calendar are largely mechanical; the investigation is judgement.

processes.description: Prior month adjustment sheets are distributed to the scheduling and trading desks, who are asked to help clear them. Reviewers question individual items, such as why a counterparty change cut revenue or why a reduction in purchased energy produced a charge, and price revisions are explained back. Items needing deeper investigation are forwarded on, and the reviewer reports when most of the sheet is resolved while flagging items still open.
steps: Distribute the prior month adjustment sheet and ask the desk to help clear it.
Review each adjustment and question items that do not make sense.
Explain price or volume revisions behind specific adjustments.
Forward unclear items to the person best placed to investigate.
Report the sheet as largely resolved and flag remaining open items.

stalls.summary: A large item on the sheet stayed unresolved after the rest was cleared and was still being raised as a problem.
Some adjustments could not be explained at review and were passed on for further investigation.

automation.approach: Produce the adjustment sheet with a reason code and the underlying price or volume change attached to each line, so reviewers see why an item moved without asking. Track each line's status and owner until it is cleared.
automation.rationale: Most of the mail is reviewers asking why an adjustment exists. A sheet layout with the cause and owner per line answers those questions up front and keeps open items visible.

work_estimate.rationale: A round means going through the adjustment sheet line by line, tracing price or volume revisions for the items that look wrong, and investigating unexplained charges. About 45 minutes for a sheet with a handful of questioned items; longer when a large disputed item needs tracing. Pulling the underlying changes is mechanical; deciding whether an adjustment is right is not.

processes.description: Managers announce openings for analysts, associates, trading assistants and logistics staff, ask the analyst programme for candidates or refer internal candidates, and forward resumes to the hiring group. Interview panels and times are arranged, candidates receive schedules, and interviewers send feedback. Hiring managers request specific analysts be brought into their group, add justification when replacing staff, and decline or keep applicants on file when no opening exists.
steps: Identify an opening and write or revise the job posting.
Request candidates from the analyst programme, HR or internal referrals.
Forward resumes and internal candidates to the hiring manager for review.
Agree the interview panel and schedule interviews with candidates.
Hold interviews and send feedback to the hiring manager.
Request the selected analyst or candidate be placed in the group, with justification where needed.
Reply to unsuccessful or unsolicited applicants.

stalls.summary: Interviews were missed or cancelled by interviewers and had to be rearranged.
A manager resisted releasing an analyst another group wanted, holding up the placement.
Feedback waited on interviews not yet held, and replacement hires required written justification before going ahead.

contradictions.summary: Two groups pulled in opposite directions over the same analyst: one side pressed to move him while his current manager refused to give him up unless forced.

automation.approach: Use a standard opening request form and posting template, a shared interview scheduler that collects interviewer availability once, and a candidate tracker that records resumes, panel, feedback and decision for each opening.
automation.rationale: Rounds repeat the same pieces: posting text, candidate lists, panel availability, schedules and feedback. A request and tracking template cuts the back-and-forth over availability and keeps feedback and justification with the opening.

work_estimate.rationale: A round typically involves writing or revising a posting, reviewing resumes or an internal candidate, and arranging a panel and interview schedule; some rounds include the interview itself. About 40 minutes for reviewing candidates and building a schedule; up to 120 when interviews are held. Scheduling and posting are templatable; assessing candidates is not.
